findings.title: Security group ingress open to the world
findings.description: Ingress rules allowing 0.0.0.0/0 expose the workload to the entire internet. Restrict source CIDRs to known ranges.
findings.remediation:
Restrict the ingress CIDR to trusted ranges. Replace `0.0.0.0/0` with your
office/VPN CIDRs, or remove the rule and use SSM Session Manager (no inbound
SSH needed):
ingress {
  from_port   = 22
  to_port     = 22
  protocol    = "tcp"
  cidr_blocks = ["203.0.113.0/24"]  # your trusted range
}

findings.title: RDS instance without storage encryption
findings.description: RDS storage should be encrypted at rest. The provider default for storage_encrypted is false, so an absent attribute is a finding.
findings.remediation:
Enable storage encryption on the RDS instance:
resource "aws_db_instance" "this" {
  # ...
  storage_encrypted = true
  kms_key_id        = aws_kms_key.rds.arn  # optional CMK
}
Note: encryption cannot be enabled on an existing unencrypted instance —
take a snapshot, copy it with encryption, and restore.

findings.title: RDS instance publicly accessible
findings.description: A publicly accessible database accepts connections from the internet. Keep databases in private subnets with publicly_accessible false (the provider default).
findings.remediation:
Set `publicly_accessible = false` and move the database to private subnets:
resource "aws_db_instance" "this" {
  # ...
  publicly_accessible = false
  db_subnet_group_name = aws_db_subnet_group.private.name
}
Access the database via a bastion host, VPN, or SSM port forwarding — never directly.

findings.title: Hardcoded credentials in resource config
findings.description: A database password written as a literal in Terraform config is stored in state, plan output, and version control. The same holds for a secret-like variable or local flowing into a credential attribute. Reference a secrets manager or a generated password instead. The secret value is never included in findings.

evidence.expected: reference to a secrets manager or generated password

findings.remediation:
Remove the hardcoded credential and rotate it immediately — it is compromised.
Reference a Secrets Manager secret instead:
data "aws_secretsmanager_secret_version" "db" {
  secret_id = aws_secretsmanager_secret.db.id
}
# then: password = jsondecode(data.aws_secretsmanager_secret_version.db.secret_string)["password"]
If the value was committed to git, purge it from history (BFG/truffleHog) and rotate.

findings.title: Secrets in EC2 user_data
findings.description: A secret (AWS key, password, token) embedded in EC2 user_data is visible in the console, API responses, and instance metadata. user_data_base64 is decoded before scanning. Pass secrets via instance profiles, SSM Parameter Store, or Secrets Manager instead. The secret value is never included in findings.

evidence.actual: [REDACTED: AWS access key ID in user_data]
evidence.expected: no secrets in user_data; use instance profiles or SSM/Secrets Manager

findings.remediation:
Remove secrets from user_data immediately and rotate every exposed value.

secret ever placed there as compromised.

findings.title: Elasticsearch/OpenSearch domain without HTTPS enforcement
findings.description: A search domain whose domain_endpoint_options does not set enforce_https = true serves the cluster endpoint over plaintext HTTP, exposing credentials and query data in transit.
findings.remediation: Enforce TLS 1.2+. Replace HTTP listeners with HTTPS, set a modern TLS policy (e.g. `ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06`), and redirect HTTP→HTTPS. Disable weak ciphers and old protocol versions everywhere.

findings.title: Elasticsearch/OpenSearch domain without dedicated master nodes
findings.description: A search domain whose cluster_config does not set dedicated_master_enabled = true runs cluster coordination on data nodes, risking split-brain and instability under load. Use dedicated master nodes for production domains.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Elasticsearch/OpenSearch domain without zone awareness
findings.description: A search domain whose cluster_config does not set zone_awareness_enabled = true places all nodes in one availability zone: a zone failure takes the domain down. Enable zone awareness for multi-AZ resilience.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Elasticsearch/OpenSearch domain without snapshot configuration
findings.description: Hygiene: a search domain without a snapshot_options block has no configured automated snapshot schedule, slowing recovery from data loss or corruption. Set automated_snapshot_start_hour.
findings.remediation: Enable data protection. Turn on versioning / point-in-time recovery / automated backups with a retention period ≥ 7 days (30+ for production). Test restores regularly — untested backups are not backups.

findings.title: Elasticsearch/OpenSearch domain without slow logs
findings.description: Hygiene: a search domain whose log_publishing_options publish neither SEARCH_SLOW_LOGS nor INDEX_SLOW_LOGS hides expensive queries, blinding performance tuning and abuse detection. Publish slow logs. (Audit-specific coverage: AEGIS-AWS-618; any-log coverage: AEGIS-AWS-623.)
findings.remediation: Enable audit logging. Turn on CloudTrail (multi-region, log file validation, KMS-encrypted bucket), VPC flow logs, and service access logs. Ship logs to a dedicated, MFA-delete-protected bucket in a security account.

findings.title: Elasticsearch/OpenSearch domain on an end-of-life engine version

findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Elasticsearch domain without fine-grained access control

findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Lambda function without dead-letter queue

findings.title: Lambda function with plaintext secret in environment variables
findings.description: An aws_lambda_function environment variable holding a value that looks like a live credential (AWS key, 40-char secret, or long mixed token) exposes the secret to anyone with read access to the function configuration. }

findings.title: Compute instance boot disk without customer-managed encryption
findings.description: google_compute_instance boot_disk initialize_params without kms_key_self_link uses Google-managed disk encryption.
findings.remediation: Enable encryption at rest. For AWS-managed keys add the service's encryption block (e.g. `storage_encrypted = true` for RDS, `server_side_encryption_configuration` for S3). For regulated data use a customer-managed KMS key via `kms_key_id` and enable key rotation.
